morphCo.title: Morph & Co. KG - The Word Factory

intro.page1: For centuries, the famous word factory of Morph & Co. KG has been producing every single German word. Normally everything runs automatically: morphemes are delivered, word-formation affixes are attached, inflectional endings are mounted at the very end, and compounds are assembled.
intro.page2: This morning, however, something went wrong: some of the machines have gone haywire and are producing nonsense or have stopped working altogether. Prefixes end up on the wrong words, and inflectional endings get mixed up beyond recognition.
intro.page3: Quality control stopped production immediately, but without new words and word forms, communication chaos is just around the corner! If the company wants to deliver its orders on time, the production line has to be repaired as quickly as possible.
intro.page4: Help Morph & Co. KG get its production running again!

story.arrival: "Finally, you're here!" the shift supervisor yells over the siren. Wuuuuuuh, wuuuuuh! Waving both arms, she keeps shouting: "I...ThAla...oud!"
story.arrival-alarm: "TOO LOUD. ALARM!" She taps her ear, then points to the door with the card reader.
story.arrival-card: You pull out your security card. First the noise, then the questions.
story.hint-alarm: "TOO LOUD! ALARM! CONTROL ROOM!" That's all you can make out. She points to the door with the card reader.
story.hint-pc: "Thank you! Finally you can hear yourself think again. Please check the computer in the control room. The production control system knows what is broken."
story.hint-repair: "F-04 and A-12 are on strike. It doesn't matter in which order you repair them. The door opposite the entrance leads from the control room to the corridor. There are shelves with manuals in the halls."
story.hint-handbook: "I wouldn't touch the inflection machine without the manual. Have a look at the bookshelf in F-04."
story.hint-word-classes: "Next to the inflection machine there are crates for the inflectable parts of speech. I bet a lot of things are in the wrong place there."
story.hint-hatch: "The maintenance hatch of A-12 has a number lock. The answer is in 'Morpheme Types and Where to Find Them: Part 1'. That book is on the shelf in F-04."
story.hint-affixes: "The affixes in A-12 are jammed. Cut the affixes off the words and sort them. Words without an affix - compounds too - go undivided into the 'No affix' bin."
story.hint-flexion: "A-12 is sorting again? Then go and check whether the inflection machine is getting the right affixes now."
story.hint-restart: "Everything repaired? Great! Then off to the control room and restart production at the computer."
story.hint-done: "Do you hear that? They're running again! I never thought I'd be this happy about machine noise. Thank you!"
story.hint-shafts: "Word formation or inflection? 'Morpheme Types and Where to Find Them: Part 2' on the shelf in A-12 says it: an inflectional affix forms a new word form, a derivational affix forms a new word."

entrance.warning-sign: "Authorized personnel only!" According to your security card, that includes you.
entrance.card-slot: Beep! The door whirs open. At least something still works around here.
entrance.card-slot-open: Beep. The door is already open.
entrance.swipe-help: Drag the card through the slot from left to right with the mouse. No mouse? Hold space or the right arrow key and let go at the end. Not too fast, not too slow.
entrance.swipe-too-fast: Too fast. Try again. The device is older than you.
entrance.swipe-too-slow: Too slow. Try again. The device nodded off for a moment.
entrance.swipe-incomplete: Card not recognized. Swipe all the way through.
entrance.swipe-accepted: Access granted. Have a good shift!

control.enter: In the control room the alarm is only half as loud. To make up for it, it's twice as red in here.
control.console: Every button is labelled. The 'Annoying alarm sound' button is pressed in and trembles in time with the siren.
control.console-conveyor-result: Somewhere a conveyor belt judders a little faster. The alarm keeps wailing, unimpressed.
control.console-coffee-result: In the staff kitchen a coffee machine gurgles. Unfortunately, the kitchen is locked. The alarm keeps wailing.
control.console-music-result: Soft elevator music starts tootling in the corridor. It doesn't stand a chance against the alarm.
control.console-light-result: For a moment the emergency lighting flickers. Then everything is back to how it was - alarm included.
control.console-light-on: The emergency lighting has been on ever since the fuse box was rewired. It doesn't get any greener than this. The alarm keeps wailing anyway.
control.console-alarm-off: Silence at last! Or ... almost. Somewhere a machine is rattling, and from a ventilation shaft comes a noise that sounds suspiciously like a printer in its death throes. At least you can think straight again. Time for the computer.
control.console-done: The 'Annoying alarm sound' button is no longer pressed. And that's how it stays.
control.fuse-box: All the fuses are in. Someone has pulled out every single cable, though, and laid them out neatly side by side. That doesn't look like a loose connection.
control.fuse-box-help: Drag each cable end into the socket with the same label. Or click a cable end first and then the socket.
control.fuse-box-wrong: Wrong socket. The cable springs back.
control.fuse-box-done: All cables are in. The emergency lighting is on.
control.fuse-box-wired: Every cable is in, every lamp is lit. This box has probably never been wired this neatly. It won't tell you who pulled the cables out, though.
control.coffee: Empty. The coffee ring at the bottom looks older than the crisis.
control.plant: The soil is bone-dry. When was it last watered, I wonder?
control.cctv: "Attention, this area is under video surveillance." You can't spot a camera anywhere. Maybe that's exactly the trick.
control.table: Loose shift schedules lie between the phone and the coffee mug. Under today's date someone has scrawled: "Cover is coming (hopefully)".
control.poster1: Safety notice: Do not leave your luggage unattended.
control.poster2: Invitation to the summer party: All employees are cordially invited to this year's summer party. 12 June, 4:30 pm, behind the classifier control towers. Potluck buffet as always (NO quiches, we all still remember last year!!!) - Bring FUN! - signed, the Summer Party Committee
control.poster3: "Safety starts with you. Work safely, get home safely!"
control.poster4: Employees of the Bound Morphemes department are asked to reliably clock in before their shift starts! Clocking in retroactively is not possible!
control.phone: You pick up the receiver. It beeps impatiently in your ear.
control.phone-quiet: You pick up the receiver. Dial tone.
control.phone-message: "You have one new message. First new message, received at 1:31 pm: Wuuuuuuh, wuuuuuh, wuuuuuh, wuuuuuh."
control.phone-security-result: Beeep ... beeep ... beeep ... Nobody picks up at the security desk.
control.phone-rosi-result: Beeep ... beeep ... beeep ... Whoever Rosi is: she's not picking up.

corridor.kitchen: The staff kitchen is locked. Through the gap in the door you can smell cold coffee.
corridor.storage: The storage room is locked. What could be in there?
corridor.sign-kitchen: Staff kitchen - access during breaks only
corridor.clock: Production has been at a standstill since 1:37 pm, but the clock keeps ticking.

restroom.sink: You quickly wash your hands. Hygiene matters, even in a crisis.
restroom.mirror: In the mirror you see a person who is about to save an entire word factory. No pressure.

f04.sign: "From one lexeme, many word forms - since 1785."
f04.enter: This is where lexemes are supposed to be reliably turned into the right word forms. Instead, a machine is squeaking as if it had a toothache.
f04.plant: A potted plant. What did you expect?
f04.conveyor-word: "$1"? Nobody talks like that. Apparently the machine is attaching the wrong inflectional endings.
f04.conveyor-word-fixed: "$1" - This reject stays a reject. But the new word forms are coming out of the machine correctly again.
f04.conveyor: Nothing but rejects on the belt: du schreiben, Gemäuse, undes, zerkleinst. You can examine the word forms, but you can't repair them yet.
f04.poster1: Conjugate, decline, form comparatives: we get everything into (word) form.
f04.poster2: ATTENTION: Word-formation morphemes have no business in the inflection line!
f04.screen-fixed: READY. Below it, in tiny letters: "Thank you."
f04.trash-instruction: Crumpled production slips, right up to the rim. Maybe there's something useful underneath.
f04.trash-help: Drag the slips out of the basket or click one to toss it out. Click a folded sheet to unfold it.
f04.trash-rejects: More rejects: $1. So the machine didn't just start acting up today.
f04.trash-report: Repeated misassignment of inflectional suffixes. Technical inspection urgently recommended.
f04.shelf: You run a finger along the spines. Which book do you open?
f04.book-green-text: The book really is green. Inside, it's all about syntax. Exciting, but not your problem right now.
f04.book-zero: The Three Zero Morphemes and the Lost Form
f04.book-zero-text: A crime novel. You leaf through it: the pages are blank. Somehow fitting.
f04.book-evidentia-text: A collection of stories from the word factory. No time for story hour right now.
f04.book-morph1: Morpheme Types and Where to Find Them: Part 1
f04.crates-locked: The crates are labelled, but what goes in - and what doesn't? You should find some instructions first.
f04.crates-done: The crates are neatly filled. Only inflectable parts of speech get into the inflection machine now.
f04.crates-solved: All correct! Only inflectable words are in the crates. The inflection machine is now being supplied with the right parts of speech.
f04.machine-locked: You reach for the first button and hesitate. Who knows what you might set off. You should first find something that can help you here.
f04.machine-inspect: You compare what comes out of the machine with the manual. It looks as if both the wrong affixes and the wrong parts of speech are being delivered here. Find out how that can happen.
f04.machine-need-crates: The affixes are right now. But the wrong parts of speech are still ending up in the machine. Take a look at the crates next to the machine.
f04.machine-need-a12: The parts of speech are right now. But the machine is still being supplied with the wrong affixes. The affix sorting unit A-12 needs to be repaired.
f04.machine-repaired: You produce a few new word forms as a test: grammatisches, Möwen, vergleichst. Wonderful! The right parts of speech, the right inflectional affixes - no more trace of strange formations with uninflectable words, derivational suffixes or prefixes!
f04.machine-done: The inflection machine hums contentedly to itself.
f04.crates-solved-a12: All correct! Only inflectable words are in the crates. The inflection machine is now being supplied with the right parts of speech. Now try the inflection machine!

a12.poster: WARNING: Morphemes are not edible! Please do not eat!
a12.picture: Judging by how relaxed the marmot looks, it hasn't heard about the production stop yet.
a12.shelf: You run a finger along the spines. Which book do you open?
a12.book-syntagma-text: An adventure novel about sentence constituents. Sounds exciting, but that's a different chapter.
a12.book-morph2: Morpheme Types and Where to Find Them: Part 2
a12.book-hamster: 100 Sophisticated Hamster Jokes for Everyday Use
a12.machine: There is a clacking inside, as if something were stuck.[n]The display reads: "Sorting error. Manual inspection required. Open maintenance hatch."
a12.machine-sorting: The display reads: "Sorting blocked. Sort affixes manually."
a12.machine-repaired: The affix sorting unit is running again. Plop, plop, plop: every affix lands in the right category.
a12.lever-repaired: The lever now moves effortlessly. Clack. Clack. Still, nothing happened.
a12.lock-question:
How many different types of free morphemes
(not counting the portmanteau morpheme) are distinguished?
Enter a number to unlock the lock.
a12.lock-wrong: The lock beeps grumpily. That wasn't the right number.
a12.lock-correct: Click! Now the maintenance hatch can be opened.
a12.lock-open: The lock already got its number. It wants nothing more from you.
a12.hatch-locked: The hatch doesn't give an inch. The electronic lock next to it wants a number first.
a12.hatch-open: You open the maintenance hatch. Inside, affixes have got jammed into each other and are blocking the sorting. No wonder the assignments are wrong! Sort the affixes to get the unit running again.
a12.affixes-solved: You have identified all affixes correctly! Now sort the prefixes, suffixes and circumfixes into the input shafts for word formation or inflection, depending on where they belong.
a12.shafts-solved: With a soft plop, plop, plop you can hear the sorting machine sorting the affixes into the right categories again. Now the inflection machine should be supplied with the correct affixes again, too!
a12.hatch-done: Behind the maintenance hatch everything is neatly sorted.
a12.pile: You rummage through the odds and ends and find circumfixes, some intact, some broken. Do you want to take some with you?
a12.pile-taken: You get some broken circumfix pieces. The boundary hyphen is missing - it must have broken off ...
a12.pile-empty: Only odds and ends that nobody can do anything with are left here.
a12.station-empty: The station's three small bowls are empty. You don't have any suitable parts.
a12.station-done: In the middle bowl lie three freshly assembled circumfixes: {ge- ... -e}, {be- ... -ig} and {ge- ... -en}.
a12.station-wrong: The pieces don't fit together like this. The middle bowl stays empty.
a12.station-missing: You're missing one of the two pieces.
a12.station-assembled: $1 appears in the middle bowl - as in "$2".
a12.lock-almost: The lock beeps grumpily. Almost - but the portmanteau morpheme does not count.

documents.handbook: The inflection machine FL3-10-9001 is responsible for the inflection of words. Alongside word formation, inflection is a subfield of morphology; it deals with how new word forms are built.[n][n]The inflectable parts of speech are [color=#1f5fa8]nouns, adjectives, verbs, articles and pronouns[/color]. Attention: only these parts of speech may go into the inflection machine! Deliveries containing adverbs, particles, conjunctions or prepositions must not be stored together with the inflectable parts of speech![n][n]In German, inflection is realized by means of affixes, especially suffixes (geh-st, schreib-en, Hamster-s), and by changes to the word stem, for example ablaut (gehen - ging - gegangen) or umlaut (Buch - Bücher). Attention: [color=#a8321f]prefixes and circumfixes therefore do not belong in the inflection machine![/color][n][n][color=black]Did you enjoy this book? Then also buy: Morpheme Types and Where to Find Them, our new bestseller in two volumes![/color]

documents.source: Overview adapted from Busch, Albert & Oliver Stenschke (2014). Germanistische Linguistik. Eine Einführung. Tübingen: narr, p. 83.

hamster-jokes.subtitle: Classy humor with a pinch of irony, philosophical depth and the occasional pun - for people who can laugh about hamsters without going round the bend.
hamster-jokes.chapter-2: 2. Hamster Jokes for the Office and Working Life (21-40)
hamster-jokes.chapter-5: 5. Quick-Witted Hamster Sayings for Every Day (76-90)
hamster-jokes.joke-1: Why does the hamster study philosophy? - Because he wants to know whether he is running in the wheel or the wheel is turning around him.
hamster-jokes.joke-2: What does a hamster say to Descartes? - "I think, therefore I hoard."
hamster-jokes.joke-3: Why does the hamster read Kant? - Because he finally wants to understand what a categorical gnawing imperative is.
hamster-jokes.joke-4: What is a hamster's greatest insight? - That progress does not necessarily involve a change of location.
hamster-jokes.joke-5: Why is the hamster an existentialist? - He runs in circles every day and calls it free choice.
hamster-jokes.joke-6: What does a hamster say at the philosophy congress? - "The world is small. My cage confirms it."
hamster-jokes.joke-7: Why does the hamster doubt reality? - Because his wheel has made more revolutions than his worldview.
hamster-jokes.joke-8: What is the theory of relativity for a hamster? - Five minutes at the vet take longer than five hours in the grain store.
hamster-jokes.joke-9: Why does the hamster like Socrates? - Because he, too, knew that he knew nothing. Especially about where his sunflower seeds were.
hamster-jokes.joke-10: How does a hamster define infinity? - As the distance he covered in his wheel yesterday.
hamster-jokes.joke-11: Why is the hamster interested in epistemology? - He wants to know whether a hidden grain still exists once he has forgotten it.
hamster-jokes.joke-12: What does the hamster say to Nietzsche? - "If you stare into the wheel long enough, the wheel eventually spins back."
hamster-jokes.joke-13: Why is the hamster a skeptic? - Because he assumes on principle that behind every friendly hand there is a pet carrier.
hamster-jokes.joke-14: What does the hamster understand by dialectics? - Thesis: I am hungry. Antithesis: I have supplies. Synthesis: I am hungry anyway.
hamster-jokes.joke-15: Why did the hamster never write an autobiography? - His life was full of repetition.
hamster-jokes.joke-16: What is the difference between a philosopher and a hamster? - The philosopher goes round in circles in his head. The hamster at least gets some exercise out of it.
hamster-jokes.joke-17: Why is the hamster interested in metaphysics? - Because the physics of his wheel is too obvious to him.
hamster-jokes.joke-18: What did the hamster say about free will? - "Of course I'm free. I could stop running any time I like. Tomorrow, maybe."
hamster-jokes.joke-19: Why does the hamster understand Stoicism? - Because he has learned to accept external circumstances. Except for the sound of the vacuum cleaner.
hamster-jokes.joke-20: What is the philosophy of life of an educated hamster? - "Carpe diem. Conserva grana." - Seize the day. Stash the grain.
hamster-jokes.joke-21: Why was the hamster promoted to CEO? - He had years of experience in making everyone look busy without getting anywhere.
hamster-jokes.joke-22: What does the hamster say in the job interview? - "My greatest strength? I can stay in the wheel even under pressure."
hamster-jokes.joke-23: Why does the hamster work in accounting? - Because he counts every peanut twice.
hamster-jokes.joke-24: What is a hamster manager's favorite word? - "Closed-loop optimization."
hamster-jokes.joke-25: Why was the hamster never fired? - Nobody else could fake being busy so convincingly.
hamster-jokes.joke-26: What does the hamster say after eight hours in the wheel? - "A productive day. We are exactly where we started."
hamster-jokes.joke-27: Why did the hamster found a start-up? - He wanted to turn his hamster wheel into a scalable business model.
hamster-jokes.joke-28: What does the hamster call unpaid overtime? - Personal wheel development.
hamster-jokes.joke-29: Why does the hamster prefer working from home? - His commute is seven centimeters.
hamster-jokes.joke-30: What does a hamster say at the interview for a management position? - "I bring extensive experience in stockpiling and crisis management."
hamster-jokes.joke-31: Why does the hamster attend a time management seminar? - So he can run in circles more efficiently.
hamster-jokes.joke-32: What is the motto of the hamster HR department? - "We're not looking for go-getters. We're looking for go-rounders."
hamster-jokes.joke-33: Why did the hamster get a raise? - Because his cheeks were stuffed with arguments.
hamster-jokes.joke-34: What does a hamster say before a presentation? - "I'll keep it short. My remarks will go round in circles anyway."
hamster-jokes.joke-35: Why did the hamster become a management consultant? - He could explain to any company why it had to spin faster.
hamster-jokes.joke-36: What is the difference between a hamster wheel and an office? - In the hamster wheel, at least you notice that you're running in circles.
hamster-jokes.joke-37: Why does the hamster love Excel? - At last he can stash his supplies in spreadsheets.
hamster-jokes.joke-38: What does the hamster say to his boss? - "I'm not overworked. I'm running at full rotational capacity."
hamster-jokes.joke-39: Why did the hamster become a project manager? - He had proven that endless processes can be kept running reliably.
hamster-jokes.joke-40: What does work-life balance mean to a hamster? - Sleeping during the day, working at night and questioning existence in between.
hamster-jokes.joke-41: My hamster claims he's a minimalist. - He owns a mere 4,000 sunflower seeds. The rest he considers reserves.
hamster-jokes.joke-42: My hamster sold his wheel. - He wanted to finally get ahead in his career.
hamster-jokes.joke-43: Why isn't the hamster an optimist? - He sees the glass neither half full nor half empty. He asks whether there's any grain in it.
hamster-jokes.joke-44: My hamster has taken up meditation. - But only until someone opens the bag of food.
hamster-jokes.joke-45: Why is the hamster so diplomatic? - He never takes sides. He fills both cheeks.
hamster-jokes.joke-46: My hamster bought a book on self-discipline. - It has been lying unopened under his supplies for three weeks.
hamster-jokes.joke-47: Why doesn't the hamster keep a planner? - He lives by the principle: what isn't eaten today gets hidden tomorrow.
hamster-jokes.joke-48: The hamster claims he has his life under control. - The wheel sees things differently.
hamster-jokes.joke-49: Why doesn't the hamster make big promises? - His reach is limited.
hamster-jokes.joke-50: My hamster wanted to consume more mindfully. - Now he looks thoughtfully at every sunflower seed before he puts it into storage.
hamster-jokes.joke-51: What is the definition of typical hamster modesty? - "I don't need much. Just a little more than everything."
hamster-jokes.joke-52: Why does the hamster always seem so busy? - Because standing still goes against his professional self-image.
hamster-jokes.joke-53: My hamster did nothing today. - He calls it strategic regeneration.
hamster-jokes.joke-54: Why is the hamster so calm? - He has carefully put his panic into storage.
hamster-jokes.joke-55: What does a hamster say when he's late? - "I was on my way, though mostly in circles."
hamster-jokes.joke-56: My hamster is an influencer now. - His first post: "Five tips for staying authentic with your mouth full."
hamster-jokes.joke-57: Why did the hamster become an art critic? - He recognizes an empty bowl at first glance.
hamster-jokes.joke-58: My hamster has started keeping a diary. - Monday: found grain. Tuesday: hid grain. Wednesday: looked for grain. Thursday: existential crisis.
hamster-jokes.joke-59: What does the hamster say about modern society? - "Everyone wants to get ahead. Nobody asks who built the wheel."
hamster-jokes.joke-60: Why doesn't the hamster like surprises? - Because he would rather stockpile supplies than expectations.
hamster-jokes.joke-61: What would Goethe's hamster drama be called? - "Feast, Part One."
hamster-jokes.joke-62: What is Shakespeare's most famous hamster question? - "To be or not to be - where could the food be?"
hamster-jokes.joke-63: Why does the hamster read Kafka? - Because he feels trapped in an opaque system.
hamster-jokes.joke-64: What does the hamster say about a Wagner opera? - "Three hours? My grain supply won't last that long."
hamster-jokes.joke-65: What is Hamlet called when hamsters perform it? - "To gnaw or not to gnaw."
hamster-jokes.joke-66: Why does the hamster admire Beethoven? - Because he created masterpieces despite great obstacles. The hamster, on the other hand, barely makes it over the rim of his bowl.
hamster-jokes.joke-67: What book does a hamster write about his life? - "One Hundred Years of Solitude in a Single Enclosure."
hamster-jokes.joke-68: Why is the hamster interested in modern art? - Because he finally wants to sell his crumpled paper strips as an installation.
hamster-jokes.joke-69: What is the title of a hamster crime novel? - "The Missing Sunflower Seed - a Case for Hercule Pawrot."
hamster-jokes.joke-70: What does a well-read hamster say at breakfast? - "Grub first, then ethics."
hamster-jokes.joke-71: Why did the hamster become a writer? - He always had a story in store.
hamster-jokes.joke-72: What do you call a hamster who writes poems? - A rodent laureate.
hamster-jokes.joke-73: What is a tragic hamster epic? - The search for a grain that is already in your own cheek pouch.
hamster-jokes.joke-74: Why does the hamster like Greek mythology? - He considers Sisyphus a distant relative.
hamster-jokes.joke-75: What does the hamster say about an abstract painting? - "Interesting. But where's the feeding station?"
hamster-jokes.joke-76: "I'm not going round in circles. I'm consistently examining every perspective."
hamster-jokes.joke-77: "I'm not a loner. I practice selective social management."
hamster-jokes.joke-78: "My supplies are not excessive. Your planning for the future is merely inadequate."
hamster-jokes.joke-79: "I don't put things off until tomorrow. I put them into professional interim storage."
hamster-jokes.joke-80: "My wheel is not a prison. It's a gym with excellent location loyalty."
hamster-jokes.joke-82: "Waste not, want not. Hoard lots, want lots."
hamster-jokes.joke-83: "There's no chaos in my enclosure. I have a dynamic filing system."
hamster-jokes.joke-84: "I don't talk with my mouth full. I argue from reserves."
hamster-jokes.joke-85: "I'm not nocturnal. I work outside society's core hours."
hamster-jokes.joke-86: "You can't have everything. But you can try to store everything."
hamster-jokes.joke-87: "I'm not suspicious. I carry out preventive risk analysis."
hamster-jokes.joke-88: "My life is not a hamster wheel. It's a long-term rotation project."
hamster-jokes.joke-89: "I'm not afraid of change. Only of changes to my meal plan."
hamster-jokes.joke-90: "Modesty is a virtue. Stockpiling is a necessity."
hamster-jokes.joke-91: A hamster goes to see a psychologist.[n]"What's troubling you?"[n]"I have the feeling that I'm not getting anywhere."[n]"And what do you do for a living?"[n]"I work in the cycle industry."
hamster-jokes.joke-92: Two hamsters are discussing economic policy.[n]"I believe in unlimited growth."[n]"But our pantry is finite."[n]"Then we simply need a bigger pantry."
hamster-jokes.joke-93: A hamster visits a motivational coach.[n]"You have to leave your comfort zone!"[n]"Interesting. My comfort zone is a wheel, and it's already moving."
hamster-jokes.joke-94: A hamster asks a scientist:[n]"If I run ten kilometers every day, where will I be after a year?"[n]"Best case, very fit."[n]"So, back here."
hamster-jokes.joke-95: Two hamsters are talking about artificial intelligence.[n]"Do you think machines could replace us?"[n]"Only if they learn to hide food in completely illogical places."
hamster-jokes.joke-96: A hamster goes to the bank.[n]"I'd like to diversify my assets."[n]"What investments do you hold?"[n]"Sunflower seeds under my little house, sunflower seeds behind the wheel and sunflower seeds in my sleeping nest."[n]"That's not diversification."[n]"Yes, it is. Three locations."
hamster-jokes.joke-97: What does a hamster say at a scientific conference on sustainability? - "I use every grain several times: as food, as an investment and occasionally as a seat."
hamster-jokes.joke-98: A hamster is asked what he thinks of globalization.[n]"Positive, in principle. But the supply chain shouldn't be longer than two meters."
hamster-jokes.joke-99: A hamster meets a time researcher.[n]"Can you change the past?"[n]"No."[n]"Pity. Then I'll just have to accept that I ate all the pumpkin seeds yesterday."
hamster-jokes.joke-100: A hamster stands in front of his wheel and announces:[n]"After years of intense self-reflection, I have finally found the meaning of life."[n]The other hamsters ask eagerly: "And?"[n]"It's not about how fast you run, but whether you have enough seeds along the way."[n]A short silence.[n]"And it took you eight years to figure that out?"[n]"No. It took the wheel eight years."
hamster-jokes.wisdom: "Life is like a hamster wheel: sometimes you go nuts, sometimes you go round in circles - and sometimes you should just step out and enjoy a sunflower."

word-classes.title: Crates next to the inflection machine
word-classes.instruction: Sort the words in the following sentences into the matching crates by their part of speech. If there is no crate for a word, just leave it where it is. That way only inflectable words end up in the crates - exactly the ones that belong in the inflection machine.
word-classes.help: Drag a word onto a crate, or click the word first and then the crate. Clicking a word in a crate puts it back.
word-classes.feedback: Not quite. In a wrong crate: $1 · inflectable but still on the table: $2
word-classes.feedback-misplaced: Not quite. In a wrong crate: $1
word-classes.feedback-missing: Not quite. Inflectable but still on the table: $1

affixes.title: Affix sorting unit A-12 - Maintenance mode
affixes.instruction: Decide whether the following words contain affixes. If they do, sort them correctly.
affixes.help: Click between two letters to cut a word at that point (another click joins it back together). Then drag each affix into its compartment, or click the piece first and then the compartment. A word without an affix goes into the "No affix" compartment as a whole. Stems simply stay where they are. For a circumfix, put both parts into the "Circumfixes" bin.
affixes.feedback: Handled correctly: $1 of $2 words. The marks on the right show which words are already right.
affixes.shafts-title: Affix sorting unit A-12 - Input shafts
affixes.shafts-instruction: Sort the prefixes, suffixes and circumfixes into the input shafts for word formation or inflection, depending on where they belong.
affixes.shafts-help: Drag each affix into a shaft, or click the affix first and then the shaft.
affixes.shafts-feedback: Not quite. Not in the right shaft: $1

station.title: Circumfix assembly station
station.instruction: Put one piece into the left bowl and one piece into the right bowl. If the two pieces fit together, the assembled circumfix appears in the middle bowl.

entries.handbook: Nouns, adjectives, verbs, articles and pronouns are inflectable - only these parts of speech may go into the inflection machine. Adverbs, particles, conjunctions and prepositions may not. Inflection works via affixes (especially suffixes) and changes to the word stem (ablaut, umlaut). Prefixes and circumfixes do not belong in the inflection machine.
entries.morph1: Lexical: verbal base morpheme {komm}, nominal {Fisch}, adjectival {schön}, adverbial {bald}.[n]Grammatical: pronominal base morpheme {ihr}, prepositional {auf}, conjunctional {und}, article {das}.[n]Portmanteau morphemes: {im} (= in dem), {beim} (= bei dem).
entries.morph2: Lexical: unique (cranberry) morpheme {Brom-}, {-thek}; verbal base morpheme if the stem does not occur as an imperative.[n]Inflectional affixes (new word form): circumfix {ge-} + {-t}, suffix {-t}/{-et}.[n]Derivational affixes (new word): prefix {un-}, {ver-}; circumfix {ge-} + {-e}, {be-} + {-t}; suffix {-ei}, {-ung}.

entries.lock-question: Question on the lock of the maintenance hatch: How many different types of free morphemes (not counting the portmanteau morpheme) are distinguished?
